title: He goes before you (Mark 16:7)
hook: the angel's words: he goes ahead of you, you'll see him there
tomorrow: what can you see from the top that you missed on the climb?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the blessing to carry: bless and keep, shine and be gracious, lift up and give peace, worded for one person at a time.
screen: `THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.`

segments.voice: A first day, a move, a goodbye: excited and terrified about the same thing, and the two feelings refuse to take turns. Mark's Easter morning holds both. At sunrise, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome walk to a tomb with spices, worrying out loud: "Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre?" They arrive, and the stone is already rolled back. The problem they carried up the road has been handled before they got there.
screen: `EXCITED AND TERRIFIED.` → `WHO WILL ROLL THE STONE?` → `ALREADY ROLLED BACK.`

segments.voice: Inside sits a young man in a white garment. "Be not affrighted," he says. "He is risen; he is not here." Then a message: "But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you." Look at three pieces. And Peter. Days before, Peter had denied knowing Jesus; the message names him on his own. Goeth before you: not waiting for them to catch up, already on the road ahead. As he said unto you: on the night of his arrest Jesus had quoted the prophet, "I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered," and in the same breath, "after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee." The promise was made knowing they'd scatter. Then Mark adds something honest: the women flee, trembling, "for they were afraid." Fear and good news on the same morning, in the same people. Christians hear Easter hope in this line: the road ahead isn't empty; someone has gone on in front. And notice where he goes. Galilee, where it all began, by the lake with the nets. The road forward runs through ordinary places, with him already there.
screen: `AND PETER.` · `ALREADY ON THE ROAD AHEAD.` · `PROMISED THE NIGHT THEY SCATTERED.` · `FOR THEY WERE AFRAID.` · then, large: `HE GOES BEFORE YOU.`

segments.voice: Stand or sit facing the door you'll walk out of next. Let one thing ahead of you come to mind, tomorrow, next week, a hope you haven't said out loud, and hold it there in front of you, without flinching, the way a road looks when someone has gone on ahead.
He goes before you. The message at the empty tomb: already on the road, ahead of the disciples and Peter, waiting in Galilee.
Keep this: he goes before you, a promise made on the night they all scattered. That's day seventeen-ninety.

screen: `DAY 1790 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 39 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT CAN YOU SEE FROM THE TOP THAT YOU MISSED ON THE CLIMB?`

howItsDone: Churches read Mark's account of the empty tomb among the Easter readings, and some Christians greet one another at Easter with 'He is risen,' a line from this same scene.

fork.setup: your cousin let down his whole team and is sure he's "out" for good. what detail in Mark 16:7 speaks to that?
options: the stone: problems simply roll away by themselves.
'and Peter': the one who denied him, named on his own.
the spices: keep doing your duty and don't think about it.
fork.reveal: Peter had denied knowing Jesus (Mark 14:66–72). the first message from the empty tomb singles him out by name: and Peter.

original.note: Greek: he goes ahead, he leads the way. the verb behind 'he goeth before you' in Mark 16:7.

trapdoor: what you thought: Easter is about the empty tomb, and that's the end of it.
what it means: a promise to frightened, scattered people that someone has gone on ahead.
what a scholar hears: Mark uses the same verb, προάγω, at 14:28 and 16:7: the promise and its keeping.

walking behind you to keep watch on you

a few plain lines to walk by

chat.says: orientation saturday. first time anywhere alone. excited AND terrified. is that normal or is it a sign?
options: Both fit. Mark's women ran from the tomb afraid, carrying the best news. He goes before you.
Only the excitement counts. If you truly trusted God, the fear would be gone by now.
It's a sign. Fear means it's the wrong road; peace is how you know where to go.
chat.meaning: Mark's Easter morning holds fear and good news together, and the message is that he goes before them: someone already on the road ahead.

Mary Magdalene.meaning: a follower of Jesus, among the women at the tomb

Salome.meaning: one of the women who came to the tomb

Galilee.meaning: the region where Jesus first called his disciples
